courses.subject: HUM
courses.title: Introduction to the Humanities I
courses.description: A foundation course in the humanities for adult learners in the Odyssey program. Team-taught by faculty with humanities expertise, it focuses on close, attentive, and critical readings of key texts, images, and artefacts drawn from the humanities, arts, and related fields. The course engages students in entry-level disciplinary and multi-disciplinary humanities inquiry, and provides academic skill-building, including critical thinking and writing. Approved for Letter and S/U grading.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to adult students in the Odyssey program.

courses.subject: HUM
courses.title: Introduction to the Humanities II
courses.description: A foundation course in the humanities for adult learners in the Odyssey program. Team-taught by faculty with humanities expertise, it focuses on a variety of fictional and nonfictional material, including but not limited to the novel, poetry, autobiography, memory-work and oral history, that make up the building blocks of humanistic inquiry. The course engages students in the disciplinary and multi-disciplinary methods through which humanists engage these forms and formats, and provides academic skill building, including critical thinking and writing. Approved for Letter and S/U grading.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to adult students in the Odyssey program.

courses.subject: HUM
courses.title: Careers for Humanities Majors
courses.description: Humanities majors will prepare for their professional lives while they explore the many forms those might take. Field trips to local organizations and businesses, networking opportunities, and invited speakers will expose students to the pathways between humanities fields and the postgraduate world. This course will prepare students to translate the skills they gain in their major to a wide range of careers. Students may not receive credit for both SLAV 300 and HUM 275.
courses.prereqText: Restricted to students with junior or senior standing in the following majors: African-American Studies, Art History, Asian American Studies, Classics, Comparative and World Lit, Creative Writing, East Asian Languages and Cultures, English, Gender and Women’s Studies, German, History, French, Italian, Jewish Studies, Latino/Latina Studies, Linguistics, Philosophy, Portuguese, Religion, Russian Language and Literature, Slavic Studies, Spanish.

courses.subject: HUM
courses.title: Individual Study
courses.description: Supervised reading and research on interdisciplinary humanities topics chosen by the student in consultation with a faculty member. May be repeated to a maximum of 8 hours.
courses.prereqText: Consent of humanities adviser (An approved Learning Agreement must be submitted to 2002 Lincoln Hall, 702 S. Wright Street, Urbana, not later than the second week of the semester or the first week of the summer session).

courses.subject: HUM
courses.title: Senior Thesis
courses.description: Individual research for majors in humanities leading to the completion of a thesis. 0 to 4 undergraduate hours. No graduate credit. May be repeated to a maximum of 8 hours.
courses.prereqText: Senior standing, a declared option in humanities major, and consent of advisor.

courses.subject: HUM
courses.title: Special Advanced Topics
courses.description: Offers interdisciplinary topics in the humanities; topics vary, but normally relate to the interdisciplinary areas of study within the humanities major or to the special humanities facilities (e.g., the Language Learning Laboratory). 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours. May be repeated as topics vary to a maximum of 6 undergraduate hours or 8 graduate hours.
courses.prereqText: Will vary according to topic. See Class Schedule.

courses.subject: HUM
courses.title: Special Topics Senior
courses.description: Interdisciplinary seminar and tutorial in selected topics related to one of the options in the humanities major. 3 undergraduate hours. No graduate credit. May be repeated to a maximum of 6 hours.
courses.prereqText: Senior standing and consent of humanities adviser (Tutorial students must submit an approved Learning Agreement to 2002 Lincoln Hall, 702 S. Wright Street, Urbana, not later than the second week of the semester or the first week of the summer session).
